func_8022075C_5DBC2C.title: Accept an alternate NPC conversation
func_8022075C_5DBC2C.summary: Tests a local NPC interaction and, when accepted, transfers the task into the native conversation sequence.
func_8022075C_5DBC2C.declaration: extern int func_8022075C_5DBC2C(void *task, int value_x, int value_z);

parameters.name: task
parameters.description: Live NPC task participating in the local interaction.

parameters.name: value_x
parameters.description: Signed scalar converted to float and stored for the accepted conversation sequence.

parameters.name: value_z
parameters.description: Second signed scalar converted to float and stored for the accepted conversation sequence.

func_8022075C_5DBC2C.returns: One when the native contact test accepts the interaction; zero otherwise.
behavior: Calls the native local-contact acceptance helper first. A rejected contact returns zero without installing the conversation handoff.

On acceptance, stores the two integer arguments as floating-point conversation scalars, sets D_800C7AE2 to one, saves the task's current +0x0C callback at +0xB4, and clears velocity at +0x78, +0x7C and +0x80.

The accepted path also records the local facing value, configures the conversation animation, stores the next conversation continuation at task +0xBC, and schedules the native follow-up through the current-task scheduler.
cautions: This routine acquires client-local player control and stores live task pointers. Do not call it to reconstruct a remote NPC or a shared world checkpoint.
A set D_800C7AE2 byte does not identify which native sequence owns the lock. Observe the accepted transition that acquired it before treating a later clear as its release.
Use a live compatible NPC task in its scheduler slot. The saved callbacks and conversation fields are local pointers.
func_8022075C_5DBC2C.exampleExplanation: Observes the interaction attempt at entry and leaves acceptance, control ownership and callback installation to the original native routine.

func_80221F70_5DD440.title: Enter a local player-control lock
func_80221F70_5DD440.summary: Starts a native local-control state by setting the input lock and resetting its player-control fields.
behavior: Writes one to D_800C7AE2, clears the pointed local-player control halfword, and resets four related halfwords in the full system structure.
Sets the companion local-control state byte to one after clearing those fields. The routine takes no task argument, so its effects apply to the current local player and system state.
cautions: This is a client-local control transition, not a portable world-state setter. Do not replay it for a remote actor.
The function overwrites several local-player control fields. Call it only as part of the native sequence that owns those fields.
func_80221F70_5DD440.exampleExplanation: Observes entry without invoking the control transition a second time or altering its local-player fields.

func_80221FB0_5DD480.title: Leave a local player-control lock
func_80221FB0_5DD480.summary: Ends a native local-control state by clearing the input lock and its companion player-control state.
behavior: Writes zero to D_800C7AE2 and to the companion local-control state byte.
Also clears the pointed local-player control halfword. The function performs the release directly and does not receive an owner token or task pointer.
cautions: The routine does not prove that the caller owns the current lock. A delayed or replayed call can clear control state acquired by a newer native sequence.
Use it only at the matching native release boundary; a remote actor's phase change is not sufficient ownership evidence.
func_80221FB0_5DD480.exampleExplanation: Observes the native release without issuing another global unlock.

func_8000B4A0_C0A0.title: Reset global player-control bytes
func_8000B4A0_C0A0.summary: Clears three resident player-control state bytes during a system reset.
behavior: Clears D_800C7AE3, D_800C7AE2 and D_800C7AE0 to zero.
This resident system routine resets the three bytes together. It is broader than releasing one conversation or interaction lock.
cautions: Do not call this routine as a convenient unlock helper. It also clears other player-control and scripted-state bytes.
Observe the native reset lifecycle rather than using one cleared byte as proof that a particular actor sequence completed.
func_8000B4A0_C0A0.exampleExplanation: Observes the native system reset while leaving all three control-byte writes to the original routine.
